correctness.rationale: For each full-row-rank (n-1)-by-n real Gaussian G, null(G) is a uniform real line u. Multiplication by invertible A maps null(GA)=A^{-1}null(G). The final squared coordinate u_n^2 has Beta(1/2,(n-1)/2) law; independence across K gives exact R=kappa^2/[1+(kappa^2-1) max_j T_j]. Its maximum density behaves as (K/2)(2/B_n)^K t^{K/2-1}, proving finite inverse-q moment exactly if K>2q. Monotone convergence transfers the exact cutoff to sup over contrasts. Boundary-layer integration gives single and double rates pi kappa/B_n and 8 log(kappa)/B_n^2. For n=3 sqrt(T_j) is uniform and direct integration gives sup E R=K/(K-2) for K>=3. All domains, endpoints, and limiting quantifiers are stated; a standalone verifier cross-checks rational constructions, analytic integrals and direct Gaussian row products. No finite test substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: Independent n-1-row sketches offer a natural minimal-data null candidate but do not provide a subspace embedding, leaving exact original-residual quality unaccounted for by full-rank sketching theory. The theorem identifies a sharp, dimension-independent finite replication cutoff: the best of one/two sketches has unbounded expected relative squared residual as singular-value contrast increases, whereas three suffice; n=3 has sharp explicit constant 3 and exact finite-contrast formulas. The comparison uses an actual unsketched quality measure needed in minimum singular vector tasks and cleanly separates angular consistency from expectation control. The result does not assert runtime benefits or consequences for methods that do not use this protocol.
